title: The Bread Has 47 Names (Pain Vs Pain)
style: playful french chanson rap, 105 BPM, accordion lead, café ambient SFX, espresso machine hiss, light hip hop drums, gypsy jazz guitar, theatrical narrator, group anthem chorus, EN/FR codeswitch, parisian boulangerie vibe, list-rap pre-chorus, hooky
lyrics:
[Intro — accordion solo, café ambience, espresso machine hiss]
Madame, je voudrais… du pain
Quelle sorte de pain, monsieur?
Euh… le pain pain?
Monsieur, il y a quarante-sept sortes de pain.

[Verse 1 — playful chanson rap, French accent]
I walked into a boulangerie with confidence
I said "I would like some bread" — innocent
The baker looked at me like I asked for the moon
"Quelle sorte?" she said — and that's when I knew I was doomed

[Pre-Chorus — list-rap, building speed]
Baguette, ficelle, flûte, bâtard
Pain de mie, pain de campagne, pain au chocolat
Boule, miche, fougasse, pain complet
Couronne, épi, brioche, pain au lait

[Chorus — big anthem, group vocal]
The bread has forty-seven names!
The bread has forty-seven names!
You think you know what bread is — you don't know the bread game
The bread has forty-seven names, mon Dieu, mon Dieu, mon Dieu!

[Verse 2 — wordplay verse]
"Baguette" is a loaf, but it's also a wand
A magic baguette in Harry Potter, fais-le faire le bond
"Baguettes" plural means CHOPSTICKS — try ordering THAT in Tokyo
"Une baguette de tambour" — a DRUMSTICK — see how this goes?

[Verse 3 — false friend warning]
"Pain" in English is suffering, pain in French is BREAD
Tell a French waiter "I want pain" — he'll bring you sourdough instead
"Préservatif" looks like preservative — it's a CONDOM, beware
Don't ask for "preservatives in your bread" in Paris — the staff will stare

[Bridge — slow, romantic accordion]
Forty-seven types of bread, three meanings of baguette
Two meanings of pain, one bakery, one regret
The French language eats words like the French eat their bread
Slowly, with butter, and a little bit of dread

[Final Chorus]
The bread has forty-seven names!
The bread has forty-seven names!
You think you know what bread is — you don't know the bread game
The bread has forty-seven names, mon Dieu, mon Dieu, mon Dieu!

[Outro — spoken, accordion fade]
Une baguette, s'il vous plaît. Just one. La baguette ordinaire.
Merci. Au revoir. À demain.
